title: Five-part leukocyte entropy does not establish incremental CRP prediction in a frozen NHANES temporal transport test
abstract: We tested whether Shannon entropy of five-part leukocyte composition adds prediction of same-visit CRP>3mg/L beyond nonlinear conventional blood counts, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, adiposity and demographics. Weighted logistic models fit in NHANES2007–2008(n=5019) were frozen and evaluated in separately recruited2017–2018(n=4600). Target weighted Brier score changed from 0.17667940 to 0.17660443; delta -0.00007497, joint source/target rescaled-PSU bootstrap95% interval [-0.00027507,+0.00035049]. The registered improvement criterion was not met. Using reported differential percentages rather than rounded absolute counts reversed the point-estimate direction. This exploratory existing-data result does not support the proposed entropy term as a robust improvement over standard summaries; it neither proves absence of composition information nor evaluates future clinical outcomes.
